## 1. `main.go` — subcommand parsing

File: `/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/main.go` (99 lines total, read in full).

There is **no subcommand dispatch at all** today — no `os.Args` parsing anywhere in `main.go`, and a repo-wide grep for `os.Args` outside test files/worktrees returned nothing. The comment at `main.go:22-31` is explicit about this:

```go
// main runs the TUI. There is no subcommand any more.
//
// `dk mcp` served the MCP server on stdio (§3.38) and is gone with it (§3.61):
// the server now lives in this process, over HTTP, started by the router.
```

`main.go:32-34`:
```go
func main() {
	runTUI()
}
```

So there used to be a `switch os.Args[1]` pattern (for `dk mcp`) but it was deliberately removed — the last subcommand was folded into the TUI itself. `runTUI()` (`main.go:36-99`) does: force TrueColor env fixup, `config.Load()`, `config.EnsureConfigDir()`, `tea.LogToFile`, theme load, `app.New(cfg)`, then `tea.NewProgram(...).Run()`.

**Natural place to add `dk setup`:** in `main()`, before `runTUI()` is called unconditionally — reintroducing exactly the kind of `if len(os.Args) > 1 { switch os.Args[1] { case "setup": ... } }` that was removed for `mcp`, e.g.:
```go
func main() {
	if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "setup" {
		runSetupWizard()
		return
	}
	runTUI()
}
```
Note the comment at line 22 says "There is no subcommand any more" — reintroducing one is a real architectural reversal worth flagging/updating in that comment, not just bolting on a case.

questions and writes the resulting context via the config package's existing
`SaveContext`.

  test — `internal/forge/session/session.go:52-93`), not just stored blind.

  clone method/token), container engine, secret backend, theme. Everything

394	// applyDefaults applies the default values to a configuration.
395	// Returns an error when the file cannot be normalized — today
396	// only for registries (duplicate slug, missing parent group).
397	func applyDefaults(cfg *Config) error {
398		homeDir, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
399	
400		// `gitlab:` → `forge:`, and it runs **first**. That is not tidiness: every
401		// default below writes into cfg.Forge, so a migration placed after them
402		// would find a block that is no longer empty and take the field-by-field
403		// path — where every field is already filled with a default, and the user's
404		// own `parallel_jobs: 7` is silently dropped. Measured, not theorised: it
405		// is what the first draft did, and the retired-keys test caught it.
406		//
407		// The other half of the reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: yaml.Unmarshal
408		// is not strict here, so an un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the
409		// silence would point a context at no host at all.
410		migrateGitLabSection(cfg)
411	
412		// "dark" was a third name for the built-in theme: LoadTheme accepts "",
413		// "dark" and "default" alike, but ListThemes only ever offers "default", so
414		// a config saying "dark" named a theme no picker could show. Normalised at
415		// load; LoadTheme still accepts the old name for a file not yet rewritten.
416		if cfg.App.Theme == "" || cfg.App.Theme == "dark" {
417			cfg.App.Theme = "default"
418		}
419		if cfg.App.LogFile == "" {
420			cfg.App.LogFile = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "devdesk.log")
421		}
422		if cfg.App.DefaultView == "" {
423			cfg.App.DefaultView = "dashboard"
424		}
425		if cfg.App.WorkspacesDir == "" {
426			cfg.App.WorkspacesDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, "workspaces")
427		}
428		if cfg.App.IDECommand == "" {
429			cfg.App.IDECommand = "code"
430		}
431		// Left empty, credentials.Select already treats this as "auto"; naming it
432		// keeps the setting inside the closed set the configuration view cycles
433		// through, so the first arrow press does not jump somewhere arbitrary.
434		if cfg.App.SecretBackend == "" {
435			cfg.App.SecretBackend = "auto"
436		}
437		// Same reason: engine.Resolve reads "" as auto, but the configuration view
438		// cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to start from.
439		if cfg.App.ContainerEngine == "" {
440			cfg.App.ContainerEngine = EngineAuto
441		}
442		if cfg.Status.RefreshInterval == 0 {
443			cfg.Status.RefreshInterval = 10
444		}
445		if cfg.Status.Timeout == 0 {
446			cfg.Status.Timeout = 5
447		}
448		if cfg.Forge.Type == "" {
449			cfg.Forge.Type = ForgeGitLab
450		}
451		if cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility == "" {
452			cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility = "private"
453		}
454		if cfg.Forge.CloneMethod == "" {
455			cfg.Forge.CloneMethod = "https"
456		}
457		if cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs == 0 {
458			cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs = 4
459		}
460		if cfg.Registry.CacheDir == "" {
461			cfg.Registry.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "templates")
462		}
463		// Migrate old single-registry config to the new Registries list
464		if cfg.Registry.URL != "" && len(cfg.Registry.Registries) == 0 {
465			cfg.Registry.Registries = []RegistryItem{{
466				URL:      cfg.Registry.URL,
467				Username: cfg.Registry.Username,
468				AuthMode: AuthCredentials,
469			}}
470		}
471		if cfg.Scan.CacheDir == "" {
472			cfg.Scan.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "scans")
473		}
474		if cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports == 0 {
475			cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports = 50
476		}
477		if cfg.Scan.Timeout == 0 {
478			cfg.Scan.Timeout = 300
479		}
480		if cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans == 0 {
481			cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans = 3
482		}
483		// An address the file does not carry is the default, never "nowhere":
484		// a bind that silently does not happen would look exactly like a server
485		// that is off, and `mcp.enabled` is what answers that question.
486		if cfg.MCP.Listen == "" {
487			cfg.MCP.Listen = DefaultMCPListen
488		}
489	
490		// Auto is the historical resolution, so a config that predates the setting
491		// keeps behaving exactly as it did.
492		if cfg.Scan.TrivySource == "" {
493			cfg.Scan.TrivySource = ToolSourceAuto
494		}
495		if cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource == "" {
496			cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource = ToolSourceAuto
497		}
498		if cfg.Scan.PlumberSource == "" {
499			cfg.Scan.PlumberSource = ToolSourceAuto
500		}
501	
502		if cfg.Network.CheckTimeout == 0 {
503			cfg.Network.CheckTimeout = DefaultCheckTimeout
504		}
505		if cfg.Network.PingCount == 0 {
506			cfg.Network.PingCount = DefaultPingCount
507		}
508		if cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays == 0 {
509			cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays = DefaultCertExpiryWarnDays
510		}
511		if cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval == 0 {
512			cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval = DefaultPortsRefreshInterval
513		}
514	
515		// Backward compat: configs created before the scan-option booleans were introduced
516		// will have all of them at Go's zero value (false). Treat "all disabled" as
517		// "never configured" and apply sensible defaults so scans work out of the box.
518		//
519		// EnableCIScore is read here but never written below, and the asymmetry is
520		// the point. It is newer than the four, so a file that predates them has it
521		// false too and the migration still fires; but "the four off and CI on" is a
522		// deliberate configuration — the user asked for CI alone — and forcing vuln
523		// and secret back on would overwrite it on every load. Leaving it out of the
524		// condition is what a test caught.
525		if !cfg.Scan.EnableVuln && !cfg.Scan.EnableSecret && !cfg.Scan.EnableMisconfig &&
526			!cfg.Scan.EnableLicense && !cfg.Scan.EnableCIScore {
527			cfg.Scan.EnableVuln = true
528			cfg.Scan.EnableSecret = true
529		}
530	
531		// Last, so that the registry migrated from the legacy single-registry keys
532		// above gets a slug like every other one.
533		return normalizeRegistries(cfg.Registry.Registries)
534	}

786	// absolute pins a configured file path to one meaning.
787	//
788	// A relative gitleaks_config does not mean the same thing on both sides of the
789	// Docker boundary — DevDesk's working directory in binary mode, the container's
790	// in Docker mode — and the file is now mounted, so the two readings would
791	// disagree about which file is scanned with. Resolving it here settles it
792	// against DevDesk's own working directory, once, at load: the path that gets
793	// mounted and the path the configuration view shows are then the same string.
794	//
795	// A path that cannot be resolved is left as it was rather than dropped:
796	// RunGitleaks refuses an unreadable config with the reason, and that is a
797	// better place to fail than a config file that silently loses a setting.
798	func absolute(path string) string {
799		if path == "" {
800			return ""
801		}
802		abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
803		if err != nil {
804			return path
805		}
806		return abs
807	}

21	//
22	// Field by field, and only where the new value is empty: a file that already
23	// carries `forge:` keeps it, so a half-written file does not have its new
24	// values overwritten by its old ones. The legacy struct is cleared once read,
25	// so the key leaves the file on the next save — the precedent is

27	// `docker.network_tool_image`.

30	// un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a
31	// context at no host at all.
32	func migrateGitLabSection(cfg *Config) {
33		legacy := cfg.GitLab
34		if legacy == (GitLabConfig{}) {

16	// third language nobody speaks, and it makes the application read as an
17	// abstraction layer rather than as a tool. So every word here is the one its
18	// forge's own documentation uses.

12	type Backend string
13	
14	const (
15		// BackendKeyring is the host's own secret manager. The only backend that
16		// can promise the secret is not sitting in a plaintext file somewhere.
17		BackendKeyring Backend = "keyring"
18	
19		// BackendGitCredential delegates to git's configured credential helper.
20		// Honest only as far as that helper is: `store` writes plaintext, which is
21		// why gitHelperUsable refuses it.
22		BackendGitCredential Backend = "git-credential"
23	
24		// BackendMemory holds the secret for this session and nothing longer. It is
25		// the fallback, and it is deliberately the worst one — see Selection.Detail.
26		BackendMemory Backend = "memory"
27	)
28	
29	// Preference values accepted from app.secret_backend in the configuration.
30	const (
31		PreferenceAuto          = "auto"
32		PreferenceKeyring       = "keyring"
33		PreferenceGitCredential = "git-credential"
34	)
35	
36	// gitConfigTimeout bounds the `git config` read that inspects the helper. Same
37	// reasoning as credentialTimeout: a blocked git call must not freeze the TUI.
38	const gitConfigTimeout = 2 * time.Second
39	
40	// Selection is a storage together with the answer to "where does the secret go".
41	// The UI needs both: it has to tell the user which store a token was written
42	// to, and warn them when the answer is "nowhere that survives this session".
43	type Selection struct {
44		Storage Storage
45		Backend Backend
46	
47		// Detail is a sentence for the user, naming the store or explaining why
48		// there is none. Always populated.
49		Detail string
50	}
51	
52	// Persists reports whether a secret saved here survives the process.
53	func (s Selection) Persists() bool {
54		return s.Backend != BackendMemory
55	}

57	// Select resolves the storage for a context.
58	//
59	// The order is deliberate and there is exactly one destination — writing to
60	// several at once is what made the old "secure" option store the token in the
61	// credential manager *and* in a plaintext file (§3.9):
62	//
63	//  1. the host secret store, when one answers;
64	//  2. git's credential helper, when git is configured with one that does not
65	//     itself write plaintext;
66	//  3. memory, for this session only.
67	//
68	// preference comes from app.secret_backend and pins the head of that list.
69	// A pinned backend that turns out to be unreachable falls through to memory
70	// rather than silently to the other one: someone who asked for the keyring
71	// should not get a git helper without being told.
72	//
73	// The returned Selection must be kept for the lifetime of the context. Calling
74	// Select again yields a fresh MemoryStorage, and a token saved into the old one
75	// would be invisible to it.
76	func Select(contextName, preference string) Selection {
77		switch preference {
78		case PreferenceKeyring:
79			if KeyringAvailable() {
80				return keyringSelection(contextName)
81			}
82			return memorySelection(KeyringName() + " is configured but not reachable")
83	
84		case PreferenceGitCredential:
85			if helper, ok := gitHelperUsable(); ok {
86				return gitSelection(contextName, helper)
87			}
88			return memorySelection("git is not configured with a credential helper that stores secrets safely")
89		}
90	
91		if KeyringAvailable() {
92			return keyringSelection(contextName)
93		}
94		if helper, ok := gitHelperUsable(); ok {
95			return gitSelection(contextName, helper)
96		}
97		return memorySelection("no " + KeyringName() + " and no usable git credential helper")
98	}

100	func keyringSelection(contextName string) Selection {
101		return Selection{
102			Storage: NewKeyringStorage(contextName),
103			Backend: BackendKeyring,
104			Detail:  "Secrets are stored in the " + KeyringName() + ".",
105		}
106	}
107	
108	func gitSelection(contextName, helper string) Selection {
109		return Selection{
110			Storage: NewGitCredentialStorageWithContext(contextName),
111			Backend: BackendGitCredential,
112			Detail:  "Secrets are stored by the git credential helper (" + helper + ").",
113		}
114	}

116	// SessionOnly returns a Selection that keeps secrets in this process and
117	// nowhere else. Select falls back to it, and the router starts on it before it
118	// has resolved a real backend — a Selection is never nil, so nothing has to
119	// guard against a missing store.
120	func SessionOnly(why string) Selection {
121		return Selection{
122			Storage: NewMemoryStorage(),
123			Backend: BackendMemory,
124			Detail:  "Nothing is saved — " + why + ". You will have to authenticate again next launch.",
125		}
126	}
127	
128	func memorySelection(why string) Selection {
129		return SessionOnly(why)
130	}

132	// gitHelperUsable reports whether git has a credential helper configured that
133	// is worth delegating to, and names it.
134	//
135	// `store` is refused by name: it keeps credentials in ~/.git-credentials in
136	// plaintext, which is the failure this whole change exists to remove — moving
137	// the token from one plaintext file to another is not a fix. An unset helper is
138	// refused too, since git would then have nowhere to put the secret and would
139	// quietly succeed at storing nothing.
140	//
141	// Every other helper is accepted. There is no list of the good ones to check
142	// against: `manager`, `osxkeychain`, `libsecret`, `wincred` and any number of
143	// third-party helpers all reach a real store, and enumerating them would only
144	// mean rejecting the next one someone installs.
145	func gitHelperUsable() (string, bool) {
146		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), gitConfigTimeout)
147		defer cancel()
148	
149		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "--get-all", "credential.helper")
150		var stdout bytes.Buffer
151		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
152		cmd.WaitDelay = credentialWaitDelay
153		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
154			return "", false
155		}
156	
157		// git resolves the last helper that answers, so read them in that order and
158		// take the first usable one from the end.
159		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), "\n")
160		for i := len(lines) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
161			if name, ok := usableHelperName(lines[i]); ok {
162				return name, true
163			}
164		}
165		return "", false
166	}
167	
168	// usableHelperName extracts the helper name from one credential.helper value
169	// and reports whether it stores secrets somewhere other than a plaintext file.
170	func usableHelperName(value string) (string, bool) {
171		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
172		if value == "" {
173			return "", false
174		}
175	
176		// A value may carry arguments (`store --file=/path`), and a leading `!`
177		// marks a shell command. Only the first word names the helper.
178		name := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.Fields(value)[0], "!")
179		if name == "store" {
180			return "", false
181		}
182		return name, true
183	}

163	func (f *CreationForm) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*CreationForm, tea.Cmd) {
164		max := f.maxField()
165	
166		switch msg.String() {
167		case "esc":
168			return f, func() tea.Msg { return CreationFormCancelMsg{} }
169	
170		case "down":
171			if f.isOnTemplateField() && f.templateIdx < len(f.templates)-1 {
172				f.templateDown()
173				return f, nil
174			}
175			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField + 1) % (max + 1)
176			f.updateFocus()
177			return f, nil
178	
179		case "up":
180			if f.isOnTemplateField() && f.templateIdx > 0 {
181				f.templateUp()
182				return f, nil
183			}
184			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField - 1 + max + 1) % (max + 1)
185			f.updateFocus()
186			return f, nil
187	
188		case "enter":
189			if f.focusedField == max { // Submit button
190				return f.submit()
191			}
192			// On other fields, move to next
193			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField + 1) % (max + 1)
194			f.updateFocus()
195			return f, nil
196	
197		case "left", "right":
198			// Field 0: cycle resource type (Group ↔ Project)
199			if f.focusedField == 0 {
200				if msg.String() == "left" {
201					f.resourceType = (f.resourceType - 1 + len(f.resourceLabels)) % len(f.resourceLabels)
202				} else {
203					f.resourceType = (f.resourceType + 1) % len(f.resourceLabels)
204				}
205				f.formType = formTypeFromResourceType(f.resourceType)
206				// No focus clamp here: this branch is only reached with
207				// focusedField == 0, and maxField() never drops below 4.
208				return f, nil
209			}
210			// Field 3: cycle visibility
211			if f.focusedField == 3 {
212				if msg.String() == "left" {
213					f.visibility = (f.visibility - 1 + len(f.visibilities)) % len(f.visibilities)
214				} else {
215					f.visibility = (f.visibility + 1) % len(f.visibilities)
216				}
217			}
218			return f, nil
219		}
220	
221		// Update text inputs
222		var cmd tea.Cmd
223		switch f.focusedField {
224		case 1:
225			f.nameInput, cmd = f.nameInput.Update(msg)
226		case 2:
227			f.descInput, cmd = f.descInput.Update(msg)
228		}
229	
230		return f, cmd
231	}

16	// carried their own pair of fields, their own clear message and their own

37	// a test that inspects a Cmd carrying this timer — testutil.Msgs runs the whole
38	// batch — pays the full three seconds per assertion. internal/ui/testutil
39	// shortens it from its init, so every view test package gets that for free; the
40	// production value is what this file states and what
41	// TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds pins.

44	// Level is a footer message's severity. It decides the colour and nothing else.
45	//
46	// The three are defined by what happened, not by how it feels:

48	//	LevelError   — an operation failed, or the system refused it.
49	//	LevelWarning — the action cannot be honoured as asked, but nothing failed:
50	//	               a precondition is unmet, or it is already running.
51	//	LevelInfo    — a neutral fact, or an operation that succeeded.

72	// Status is what a view derives on every frame: a progress line, a hint, or a
73	// table loading its rows. It carries no timer — a batch outlives the three
74	// seconds a message gets, which is why the sync and prune lines were rendered
75	// from state rather than assigned to footerInfo in the first place.
76	//
77	// It is a parameter of View rather than a field of FooterMessage because it is
78	// derived, not stored: containers' action line comes from BusyLabels(), which
79	// changes with no event to push it on.
80	type Status struct {
81		Text string
82		// Spinner prepends the current spinner frame — a table loading its rows.
83		Spinner bool
84		// Level colours the line, and the zero value is LevelInfo, so a status that
85		// says nothing about it renders exactly as it always did.
86		//
87		// A derived state can be a failure as legitimately as it can be progress:
88		// "Docker unreachable" is not an event that happened once, it is what is
89		// true right now, and a message would expire after three seconds — which is
90		// D47 in one field. It needs the colour of an error and the lifetime of a
91		// state, and only Status can give it both.
92		Level Level

95	// footerMsgSeq numbers messages so a timer can name the one it was started for.
96	var footerMsgSeq atomic.Uint64

98	// ClearFooterMsg expires the message identified by ID.
99	//
100	// The ID is what makes the type safe to share across packages. Two things would
101	// otherwise go wrong: a timer started by one view could clear the message of
102	// whichever view is active when it lands, and — the bug that was already
103	// present in all eight local implementations — a message set at t+2.9s was
104	// wiped at t+3s by its predecessor's timer.

107	// PostFooterMsg puts a message in whichever footer is on screen.
108	//
109	// It exists for the router, which has none of its own: RenderFooter is the
110	// active view's (internal/app/view.go), and the one thing the router has to say
111	// — that the MCP server did not start (§3.61) — belongs on screen at startup,
112	// not in a log. Every view already offers unhandled messages to Handle, so a
113	// broadcast lands wherever the user is without any view knowing what it is
114	// about.
115	//
116	// It carries its own ID because the timer is the sender's: PostFooter builds
117	// both, so the rule that a message set without its timer never clears holds
118	// here too (Rule 128).
119	//
120	// **It lands only where a view holds a FooterMessage.** internal/ui/forge/auth
121	// renders a footer but declares none, so a broadcast posted while that view is
122	// on screen reaches nobody — and the router switches to it whenever a context
123	// has no forge credentials. That is a real gap and not a silent one: the only
124	// broadcast today is the MCP server's, and its state is also on the `mcp` tab
125	// of the configuration view, which holds it for as long as it is true rather
126	// than for three seconds. A second use of this door would need auth to declare
127	// a footer first.

134	// PostFooter builds the broadcast and the timer that expires it.
135	//
136	// For the router. A view has its own footer and calls Info, Warn or Error on
137	// it — going through here would be a second way to do what a field already
138	// does, and the message would be adopted by whatever view is active rather than
139	// by the one that meant it.
140	func PostFooter(level Level, text string) tea.Cmd {
141		if text == "" {
142			return nil
143		}
144		id := footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
145		return tea.Batch(
146			func() tea.Msg { return PostFooterMsg{ID: id, Level: level, Text: text} },
147			tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id} }),
148		)
149	}

188	// Handle consumes what the component owns and reports whether it did: a
189	// ClearFooterMsg addressed to the current message, and a PostFooterMsg from the
190	// router. A stale expiry is dropped, and so is one belonging to another view:
191	// both leave the message on screen for the time it was given.
192	func (f *FooterMessage) Handle(msg tea.Msg) bool {
193		switch msg := msg.(type) {
194		case PostFooterMsg:
195			// Adopted whole, ID included: the timer that will expire it was built
196			// with that ID by the sender, and re-numbering it here would leave a
197			// message nothing ever clears.
198			f.text = msg.Text
199			f.level = msg.Level
200			f.id = msg.ID
201			return true
202	
203		case ClearFooterMsg:
204			if f.id == 0 || msg.ID != f.id {
205				return false
206			}
207			f.Clear()
208			return true
209		}
210		return false
211	}

forms, which should keep following `CreationForm`'s single-screen

inventing a check-then-fetch two-step: a single attempt with a short

root — adding a new bundled theme file there must also add its name to
that list, or it won't be offered for download. `remoteThemeBaseURL` is a
package var (not a const) specifically so tests can redirect it to an
`httptest.Server`; don't hardcode the URL elsewhere. See
[[feedback-wizard-one-question-at-a-time]] for why this lives in a
step-by-step wizard rather than a form field.
